hints: Look closely at the atoms in the fragment, it has three carbons but that does not mean the monomer had three carbons.
Draw out poly(chloroethene) as -CH2-CHCl-CH2-CHCl- and see if you can spot -CH2-CHCl-CH2- hiding inside it.
Remember PVC is just the common name for the same polymer, then check if poly(2-chloropropene) could ever give a CHCl group.
walkthrough:
**Understand what the fragment means**

Think of this like spotting a short phrase inside a long sentence. The fragment does not have to be the repeat unit, it just has to appear when repeat units join together.

Fragment given:
$$-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-$$

**Test statement 2, poly(chloroethene)**

The monomer is chloroethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$. Addition polymerisation opens the double bond to give:
$$-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}]_n-$$
Write two repeats joined:
$$-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$$
You can clearly see $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-\text{CH}_2-$ inside it. So statement 2 is correct.

**Test statement 3, PVC**

PVC is simply the everyday common name for poly(chloroethene), poly(vinyl chloride). It has exactly the same chain as in Step 2. So statement 3 is also correct.

**Test statement 1, poly(2-chloropropene)**

The monomer is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)$. Its polymer repeat unit is:
$$-[\text{CH}_2-\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)]-$$
Every substituted carbon here is $\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)$, with a Cl and a methyl group and no H. It can never give a $-\text{CHCl}-$ group. So statement 1 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 2 and 3 are correct, statement 1 is incorrect. That combination corresponds to option C.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, but 1 is wrong because poly(2-chloropropene) contains CCl(CH3) units, not CHCl units, so it cannot contain the given fragment.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only. Statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is wrong for the reason above, and it also wrongly leaves out statement 3 which is correct.
options.C: Correct. Poly(chloroethene) gives -CH2-CHCl- repeats, and two repeats joined together contain -CH2-CHCl-CH2-. PVC is the identical polymer under its common name, so both 2 and 3 are correct while 1 is not.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only 1 is correct. In fact 1 is the only false statement. Its monomer CH2=CCl(CH3) polymerises to -CH2-CCl(CH3)- which has no CH group at all.
